Native Village of Tazlina

Tazlina’s public record in these readings centers on connections among river life, environmental work and homeland recovery. Ahtna, Incorporated’s Fall 2018 village feature describes local programmes, while Great Land Trust’s later partner account follows a 2023 land project with the Native Village of Tazlina. Their institutional perspectives and dates remain part of the story.

01

A community at the meeting of rivers

The Fall 2018 Kanas feature places Tazlina beside the Tazlina River near its confluence with the Copper River and connects its history with fishing and movement along the rivers. It distinguishes the Native Village of Tazlina’s environmental programmes from the regional corporation publishing the newsletter. This is a useful orientation to a particular community within the wider Ahtna region, without treating either institution as a substitute for the other.

Read the sources [1] Ahtna, Incorporated

02

Community visions and environmental work

The same feature follows the Council’s concern about the former Copper Valley School property and describes a 2011 workshop in which participants pictured what they wanted the place to become. Its account links discussions about land with waste reduction, recycling and community infrastructure. These are dated reports of local work and aspirations. The article’s cleanup description, completed heating project and proposed walkway should retain their 2018 context.

Read the sources [1] Ahtna, Incorporated

03

Reading a homeland-recovery partnership

Great Land Trust’s project account describes its June 2023 partnership with the Native Village of Tazlina as part of a longer effort to recover the traditional village site. The account links conservation work with continued community use and learning across generations. Tribal Administrator Marce Simeon’s quoted statement emphasizes people’s connection to this place and hopes for future generations. Read this participating organization’s narrative as one account of the project; it does not establish present title, public access or environmental conditions.

Read the sources [2] Great Land Trust

Tazlina Homeland Recovery — partner project account ↗

Publication: Undated project page; specifies 2023 project completion and June 2023 work

A project partner describes its 2023 work with the Native Village of Tazlina on homeland recovery and conservation, and quotes Tribal Administrator Marce Simeon on continuity across generations.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual complete main project-page body read through the ordinary web reader: project specifications, historical/project paragraphs and Marce Simeon’s quoted statement. Linked project map and photographs were not inspected for reuse; the underlying deeds, easements, archaeological survey and remediation files were not read.

Review recorded: November 2, 2026

Access note: Account by a participating conservation organization. Draft attributes the dated partnership narrative and future-oriented continuity aims; it does not certify current title, legal restrictions, public access, acreage, archaeological chronology, environmental condition or ecological outcomes. The page has inconsistent school acquisition/operation dates; exact school chronology is omitted. The property is marked Private.
